wild_traditional_starters.why: The owner, 2026-10-02/03: the 27 traditional starters leave the starter screen and stay wild (docs/mechanics/ENCOUNTER_DESIGN.md section 11). This is the list modpack/config/cobblemon/starters.json offered until this change, kept here because tools and tests that read the 27 from that config now have to read them from somewhere; `tools/mythical_starters.py check` requires every family to have a weighted record in data/spawns.json.
wild_traditional_starters.hisui_note: The Hisui category offered three regional forms of species already in the list (Cyndaquil, Oshawott, Rowlet), not three more families.

potent_at.why: The late one. Its only attack before the first badge is Swift (Normal, resisted by Brock's Rock types); Confusion comes at 21 and the Psychic and Steel moves through the 30s, so Cosmog trails the field until 45. Then the native final (680 BST) carries Sabrina and Blaine: Lunala's Moongeist Beam and Psychic, or Solgaleo's Sunsteel Strike.

The early one. Fighting moves arrive first (Low Sweep 6, Rock Tomb 14), so it leads Brock (Rock) and stays level-best through Misty and Surge, where Brick Break and Dig (26, 28) answer Magneton and the Electric types; after 30 it gains little until Urshifu at 45. Its scrolls are the station's to give.

The closer. A Normal-type with even stats and only Normal, Fang and Zen Headbutt coverage before 42, it is the weakest of the five through the midgame; Surf (42) and Ice Beam (44), carried into Silvally, sweep Giovanni's Ground team.

The midgame one. Poison attacks from the start (Venoshock 6, Poison Jab 16) are resisted by Brock but super effective into Erika (Grass) and resisted by her team in return, so it sweeps gym 4 alone. Sludge Bomb waits until 36 so the Erika spike is the stage-2 form's, not a stronger move's.

The Koga answer. Steel is immune to Poison, and High Horsepower (37) is super effective into Toxtricity and Drapion. Iron Head waits until 36, as Meltan's own first Steel move waits until Flash Cannon at 40 natively, so Meltan does not also sweep Erika (it walls her but cannot break her). The owner's approved 12 moves, re-levelled (owner call: see EXP-049 Results).

The moth. Bug/Fire is 4x weak to Rock, so it loses Brock outright (the owner accepts it: a Larvesta player catches something for gym 1). From 30 the grown form's Signal Beam (28) and Flamethrower (33) carry Surge and Erika; Volcarona at 45 takes Sabrina with Bug Buzz, and Quiver Dance arrives on that step (the jar's own evolution move) and in the pool at 45. Blaine is its wall. The moves lean special for Volcarona (135 SpA), though the two earlier forms keep Larvesta's physical shape, so Flame Wheel, Bug Bite and Leech Life stay.

The painter. Its movepool is what it Sketches, so it is as strong as what the player has shown it: measured 19/35 against the gym leaders (field 15-20; `python tools/mythical_starters.py measure`, 2026-10-08), Sketching only the moves of earlier gym leaders' teams and with Gen 9 Protean modelled as one type per duel. Without Protean the same Smeargle wins 9/35, so the ability is most of its strength. Erika is its best gym (4/4, Flamethrower as a Fire type) and Giovanni falls to Surf and Moonblast (5/6). The sim plays no Spore + Shell Smash line, which Sketch reaches and no Sleep Clause stops: that is EXP-065's fight against Sabrina and Lorelei, before trusting the number.

lines.moves_why: Smeargle's 1.8.0 learnset is Sketch at 1 and nine tutor, legacy and special entries (falseswipe, flamethrower, captivate, sleeptalk, furyswipes, meanlook, odorsleuth, seismictoss, spore), read from the jar's generation2/smeargle.json. Seven are spread across the levels: Fury Swipes at 1 so the level-5 starter can attack, False Swipe at 10 for catching, Seismic Toss at 20 (damage equal to its level, whatever its Attack), Mean Look at 27, Flamethrower at 33 (its one strong special move, 79 SpA at 45) and Sleep Talk at 40. Left out on purpose: Spore (the owner, 2026-10-08: Spore and Shell Smash arrive only through Sketch), Captivate and Odor Sleuth (no use here). Everything else is Sketch's: the movepool is what the player shows it.

sketch_cap.decision: The owner, 2026-10-08: Sketch kept in every form and capped at 10 uses per Pokemon ('if it is cheap, do it at 10'); docs/research/notes/sketch-cap-1.8.0.md designs it. The count rides on the Pokemon's saved dmax_level, so it goes with the Pokemon through the PC, a trade and a restart; a datapack override of Showdown's Sketch fails once it is 10; three battle callbacks count. It applies to every Pokemon that uses Sketch, wild-caught Smeargle included.
does_not_cover: a battle that ends with no callback (/stopbattle, a crash) after which the player re-slots Sketch before the next battle: that one Sketch goes uncounted (sketch-cap-1.8.0.md section 3; in the player's favour)
Mega Showdown's Dynamax Candy raises dmax_level too, so it spends a Smeargle's Sketches
an NPC trainer's Smeargle starts at 0 every battle and is never counted
